projectAttribution: Information as submitted by beneficiaries. These data are not endorsed by, and are not the responsibility of, the National Erasmus+ Office in Georgia.
projectCoverage: This snapshot covers call years 2014 to 2026. The 2026 and later call years are incomplete. Ongoing projects and source records may change.
projectMobilityCountry: Mobility projects where Georgia is listed as a participating country without a named Georgian institution
projectCountingNote: Projects are counted once by official reference. Institution participations are unique project/organisation pairs. Named organisations are counted by the source PIC/organisation identifier, excluding mobility-country entries. No project grant amounts are shown or summed.
projectSourceStatusNote: Source status is retained, rather than inferred from end dates. Completed corresponds to the source value finalized.
projectMobilityCoverage: International credit mobility with Georgia under the 2014–2020 programme (KA107) is not identifiable in the source and is not counted: Georgian partner institutions are not listed for KA107. The snapshot contains no 2014–2020 KA1 higher education mobility projects; 2021–2027 KA171 projects appear through the “Mobilities - Georgia” country entry. Year-on-year comparisons of higher education mobility across 2020/2021 are therefore not meaningful.
callsNextYear: The European Commission is expected to publish the 2027 calls in late 2026. This page will be updated when they are available.

hereIntro: Higher Education Reform Experts (HEREs) share expertise to support higher education reform in countries served by National Erasmus+ Offices. Their work includes policy development, dialogue and sharing project results. The European Commission and EACEA support the network through the SPHERE initiative.

mapDescription: Bubble area is proportional to named organisations. Select a bubble to reach its table row. Unresolved locations are shown separately above the map, without a geographic position. The outline shows Georgia’s internationally recognised borders, including Abkhazia and the Tskhinvali region/South Ossetia.
mapCounting: Each named source organisation identifier is counted once. Reviewed spelling variants are grouped by city; different cities for the same identifier are unresolved. Missing cities and places without reviewed coordinates are separate from mapped cities. These are organisation locations as submitted, not project sites or participant counts.
